input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.
input.rationale: Section 9.4 meets the preferred position on every material term: Customer (our party) may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty days' written notice; Vendor must refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period (pro-rata refund); there is no early-termination fee or penalty; and Vendor is expressly denied any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term. No redline is warranted. Noted but not flagged here: the take-or-pay language in Section 2.1 ("without reduction or termination rights") sits in tension with the Section 9.4 right and should be reconciled under the minimum-commitment rule rather than double-flagged under T4C; the conflict/precedence order in Section 2.2 and the cumulative-remedies language in Section 9.5 also support reading Section 9.4 as operative.
